name: Seoul
tagline: Royal palaces, neon nights and barbecue smoke on every corner
description:
Seoul moves at a speed that can leave you breathless, then hands you a silent palace courtyard to recover in. Joseon-dynasty palaces and tiled-roof hanok lanes sit beneath granite mountains and a skyline of glass towers, while the Han River splits the city in two, its banks lined with parks, cycle paths and picnic lawns that fill up on warm evenings.

This is a city that stays up late. Night markets, 24-hour barbecue joints, karaoke rooms and cafés with elaborate themes keep neighborhoods like Hongdae and Seongsu buzzing well past midnight, and the food ranges from sizzling pork belly and fried chicken with beer to refined temple cuisine and inventive modern Korean tasting menus.

Getting around is effortless on one of the world's best subway systems, and the city is exceptionally safe. Spring blossoms and autumn foliage are glorious; summer brings heavy monsoon rain, and winter is bitterly cold but crisp and clear. Download Naver Map or KakaoMap before you arrive, since Google Maps offers only limited directions here.

safety.notes: Seoul is very safe day and night, with little street crime. The main hazards are electric scooters on sidewalks and late-night taxi touts, so book rides through the Kakao T app.

tipping: Tipping is not customary in Korea and is sometimes politely refused; upscale hotels and restaurants already include a service charge.
gettingAround: The subway is fast, cheap and bilingual; tap a T-money card, sold at convenience stores, on trains and buses, and use Kakao T for taxis. The AREX express train links Incheon Airport to Seoul Station in about 45 minutes.
tips: Rent a hanbok near Gyeongbokgung: wearing one gets you free entry to the royal palaces, and it makes for memorable photos.
Use Naver Map or KakaoMap instead of Google Maps, which lacks full walking and driving directions in Korea.
Many barbecue and stew restaurants require a minimum of two diners; solo travelers should look for counter-seat spots or order two portions.
Instant tax refunds are available at many shops on purchases over ₩15,000, so carry your passport when shopping in Myeong-dong or Seongsu.
Book Changdeokgung's Secret Garden tour online as soon as slots open; the daily cap sells out quickly in spring and autumn.
Convenience stores are a traveler's best friend, with instant-ramyeon cooking stations, triangle kimbap and cheap beer for a fun late-night snack.
etiquette: Use both hands, or support your right arm with your left, when giving or receiving money, gifts and drinks, especially with elders.
When drinking, pour for others rather than yourself, and turn your head slightly away from elders when you sip.
Keep your voice down on the subway and leave the priority seats for elderly, disabled and pregnant passengers, even when they are empty.
Don't stand chopsticks upright in your rice or write someone's name in red ink; both are associated with death.

phrases.pronunciation: joo-seh-yo (said after the thing you want)

neighborhoods.name: Bukchon
neighborhoods.blurb: A hillside village of hundreds of tiled-roof hanok homes between two palaces, with tea houses and craft studios; residents still live here, so keep quiet.

neighborhoods.name: Ikseon-dong
neighborhoods.blurb: Tiny alleys of 1920s hanok converted into cafés, bakeries and cocktail bars; one of the most charming places in the city to eat.

neighborhoods.name: Hongdae
neighborhoods.blurb: The university district of buskers, indie clubs, cheap eats and late-night karaoke; Seoul's youthful party hub.

neighborhoods.name: Seongsu-dong
neighborhoods.blurb: A former shoe-factory district reinvented with warehouse cafés, pop-up stores and design boutiques along the Han River.

neighborhoods.name: Itaewon
neighborhoods.blurb: Seoul's most international quarter, with global cuisine, rooftop bars and the leafy hillside lanes of Haebangchon and Gyeongnidan.

dishes.name: Samgyeopsal
dishes.description: Thick slices of pork belly grilled at your table, wrapped in lettuce with raw garlic, ssamjang and kimchi, and washed down with soju.

dishes.name: Tteokbokki
dishes.description: Chewy rice cakes simmered in a sweet, fiery gochujang sauce with fish cakes; the city's favorite street snack.

dishes.name: Bindaetteok
dishes.description: Crispy mung-bean pancakes studded with pork and kimchi, fried on big griddles at Gwangjang Market and paired with milky makgeolli.

dishes.name: Naengmyeon
dishes.description: Chilled buckwheat noodles in tangy beef broth with slivers of ice; the Pyongyang style is subtle, while the Hamhung style is spicy and chewy.

dishes.name: Chimaek
dishes.description: Korean fried chicken and beer: double-fried for crunch, tossed in soy-garlic or sweet-spicy glaze, and best enjoyed at a Han River picnic.

events.name: Yeouido Spring Flower Festival
events.description: Around 1,800 cherry trees bloom along a car-free road on Yeouido island, with street performances and riverside picnics under the petals.

events.name: Lotus Lantern Festival
events.description: Ahead of Buddha's Birthday, a parade of tens of thousands of glowing lanterns flows down Jongno, and temples like Jogyesa hang thousands more.

events.name: Chuseok
events.description: Korea's harvest holiday sends families home to their ancestral towns; palaces host folk games and free events, though many shops close for three days. The date follows the lunar calendar.

events.name: Seoul International Fireworks Festival
events.description: Teams from several countries launch a dazzling show over the Han River at Yeouido; locals claim picnic spots by early afternoon. Some years it falls in late September.

attractions.name: Gyeongbokgung
attractions.description: The grandest of Seoul's five Joseon palaces is backed by the granite peak of Bugaksan, and a colorful changing-of-the-guard ceremony plays out at its main gate. The Gyeonghoeru pavilion floating on its lotus pond is one of Korea's most photographed views, and spring and autumn night openings are magical.
attractions.bookingTip: Catch the guard ceremony at 10:00 or 14:00, and wear a hanbok for free entry.

attractions.name: Changdeokgung
attractions.description: This UNESCO-listed palace follows the contours of its hillside rather than flattening them, and it was the favored royal residence for centuries. The highlight is Huwon, the Secret Garden, where ponds and pavilions hide in a wooded valley that can be seen only on a timed guided tour.
attractions.bookingTip: Reserve an English Secret Garden tour online well ahead; a limited number of same-day tickets are released at the gate.

attractions.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
attractions.description: Steep lanes of tiled-roof hanok homes climb the slope between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung, with views down to the downtown towers. This is a living neighborhood, and a curfew now bars tourists from its core lanes in the evening and early morning.
attractions.bookingTip: Arrive just after 10:00 on a weekday, keep your voice down and duck into a traditional tea house for a break.

attractions.name: N Seoul Tower
attractions.description: Perched on Namsan mountain, this tower delivers a 360-degree panorama of the city and its ring of mountains, best just after sunset as the lights come on. Hike up the forested trail or ride the cable car, and admire, or add to, the thousands of love locks on the terrace railings.
attractions.bookingTip: Walk up the Namsan trail from Myeong-dong in about 40 minutes to skip the cable-car queue, and buy observatory tickets online.

attractions.name: Gwangjang Market
attractions.description: One of Seoul's oldest traditional markets, trading since 1905, is famous for its food alley of crackling mung-bean pancake griddles, raw beef yukhoe and tiny, addictive mayak kimbap rolls. Upstairs and around the edges, fabric merchants sell silk, hanbok cloth and vintage clothing.
attractions.hours: Food stalls roughly 09:00–23:00; fabric shops closed Sun
attractions.bookingTip: Sit at stalls with clearly posted prices, grab a pancake straight off the griddle, and visit on a weekday to dodge the worst crowds.

attractions.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
attractions.description: Zaha Hadid's flowing silver landmark looks like a spaceship docked in the fashion district, with exhibition halls, design shops and a grassy rooftop walkway. At night its curved skin glows, and during seasonal light festivals it becomes a vast projection screen while the wholesale malls nearby trade until dawn.
attractions.bookingTip: Exploring the building is free; check the program online, since some exhibitions need a separate ticket.

attractions.name: National Museum of Korea
attractions.description: This vast, free museum traces Korea's story from prehistoric pottery to Joseon court painting, including golden Silla crowns and a ten-story marble pagoda standing indoors. The hushed room devoted to two pensive bodhisattva statues is unmissable.
attractions.bookingTip: General entry is free; download the museum's audio guide app and go on a Wednesday or Saturday evening when it is quieter.

attractions.name: Cheonggyecheon
attractions.description: A downtown stream once buried beneath an elevated highway now flows for nearly 11 kilometers below street level, lined with stepping stones, willows and public art. Office workers dangle their feet in the water on summer evenings, and lanterns float here during the winter light festival.
attractions.bookingTip: Start at Cheonggye Plaza and walk east toward Gwangjang Market for a dinner of pancakes and makgeolli.

attractions.name: Bongeunsa
attractions.description: Founded more than 1,200 years ago, this Buddhist temple sits in the middle of Gangnam, where monks chant beneath a towering stone Maitreya Buddha while glass office blocks loom across the street. It runs one of the city's most accessible temple-life programs for visitors.
attractions.bookingTip: Book a half-day temple-life program online for tea with a monk and a guided meditation session.

attractions.name: Bukhansan National Park
attractions.description: Granite peaks rise straight out of the city's northern edge, and a subway-plus-bus ride gets you to trailheads for the three-hour scramble to Baegundae, the 836-meter summit. Weekend trails are busy with fully kitted Korean hikers who will often share snacks and makgeolli.
attractions.hours: Trails open from before sunrise to sunset; some close in high fire-risk periods
attractions.bookingTip: Go on a weekday, start from the Bukhansanseong trailhead by 08:00 and carry plenty of water; the final section uses fixed cables.

hotels.name: Mokmyeok Hill Hotel
hotels.description: Set into the slopes of Namsan, with floor-to-ceiling windows framing the tower above and the city below, this 90-room retreat has a bathhouse-inspired spa with jade saunas and an outdoor infinity pool. Its Korean tasting restaurant is one of the hardest reservations in town.

hotels.name: Bukchon Dalbit Hanok Stay
hotels.description: Six rooms around a courtyard in a century-old hanok, with ondol heated floors, thick futons and paper-screen windows. Breakfast is a spread of rice porridge, side dishes and persimmon tea served at low tables.

hotels.name: Dongdaemun Night Owl Hostel
hotels.description: A friendly hostel with pod beds, a rooftop barbecue terrace and a shared kitchen, steps from the late-night markets around DDP and two subway lines. Instant ramyeon and coffee are free all day.

hotels.name: Ondo Seoul
hotels.description: Concrete, oak and moon-jar ceramics set the tone at this design hotel above the stream, whose lobby doubles as a gallery for young Korean artists. Rooms have rain showers and deep window seats overlooking Cheonggyecheon's evening lights.

hotels.name: Ichon Riverside Inn
hotels.description: A tidy, compact hotel in quiet Ichon-dong near the Han River, within walking distance of the National Museum and riverside bike paths. Rooms are small but spotless, with good desks and fast Wi-Fi.

hotels.name: Samseong Sky Residences
hotels.description: Serviced apartments in a Gangnam tower with full kitchens, washer-dryers and skyline views, a short walk from Bongeunsa and the COEX mall. Ideal for longer stays, families and anyone who needs a proper desk.

restaurants.name: Maetdol Bindaetteok
restaurants.description: A market stall where mung beans are stone-ground on the spot and fried in a slick of oil into crisp, thick pancakes with kimchi and pork. Pull up a stool, order a bowl of makgeolli and watch the griddle masters at work.

restaurants.name: Byeolbit Hanok Dining
restaurants.description: A twelve-course modern Korean menu served in a restored hanok facing the palace walls, where soy and bean pastes aged in courtyard earthenware jars flavor everything from hanwoo beef to abalone. Pairings of traditional soju and makgeolli are a revelation.
restaurants.signatureDish: Hanwoo galbi with five-year doenjang glaze

restaurants.name: Café Giwa
restaurants.description: A hanok café with a rooftop deck overlooking Bukchon's tiled roofs, serving hand-drip coffee, roasted-soybean injeolmi toast and herbal ssanghwa tea. Early risers get the terrace to themselves.
restaurants.signatureDish: Injeolmi toast with black sesame latte

restaurants.name: Namsan Sutbul Gui
restaurants.description: A no-frills barbecue joint at the foot of Namsan where thick-cut pork belly and neck are grilled over oak charcoal by staff who snip them with scissors at exactly the right moment. Wrap each bite in perilla leaves with a slice of garlic.
restaurants.signatureDish: Samgyeopsal and moksal over oak charcoal

restaurants.name: Seolhwa Myeonok
restaurants.description: Silver bowls of Pyongyang-style buckwheat noodles in a clear, subtly beefy broth that puzzles first-timers and hooks regulars for life. Order a plate of sliced boiled beef and a dumpling on the side.

restaurants.name: Yeonhwa Temple Kitchen
restaurants.description: Temple cuisine without garlic, onion or meat, cooked by a chef who trained with Buddhist nuns and served in lacquer bowls across the street from Bongeunsa. Seasonal mountain greens, lotus-root rice and acorn jelly are quietly brilliant.

restaurants.name: Dak-Dak Hof
restaurants.description: A buzzing beer hall in the old Euljiro printing alleys serving double-fried chicken in soy-garlic or sweet-spicy glaze with icy draft beer. Plastic stools spill out into the lane after 21:00.
restaurants.signatureDish: Half-and-half fried chicken with draft beer

restaurants.name: Trattoria Hangang
restaurants.description: A family-run Italian trattoria serving handmade pasta with Korean produce, like perilla-seed pesto and spicy clam linguine with Korean chili. A handy lunch after the museum and before a riverside bike ride.

experiences.name: Gwangjang to Euljiro Night Market Crawl
experiences.description: Graze Gwangjang's food alley with a local guide, from mung-bean pancakes to raw beef yukhoe and mayak kimbap, then follow the neon into Euljiro's hidden bars for a makgeolli tasting and a late-night bowl of noodles.

experiences.name: Palace Hanbok Photo Walk
experiences.description: Get fitted for a hanbok and hair accessories, then explore Gyeongbokgung with a photographer-guide who knows the best angles and the palace's dramatic stories of coronations, fires and intrigue.

experiences.name: Bukhansan Summit Day Hike
experiences.description: A certified mountain guide leads you to Baegundae summit by a scenic ridge route, with cable-assisted granite slabs and old fortress walls along the way. Descend to a hikers' restaurant for scallion pancakes and makgeolli, the official post-hike ritual.

experiences.name: Gangnam Zen Evening: Meditation & Tea
experiences.description: A monk-led evening of seated meditation, bowing practice with prayer beads you string yourself, and a slow tea ceremony in a hillside pavilion as Gangnam's lights flicker on around you.
